title: Beyond Wikipedia: A Technical Workshop Introducing Moroccan Teachers to Wikidata and the Wikimedia Technical Ecosystem
content:
As part of the Wikipedia in Education Workshop held in Casablanca in August 2026, I had the opportunity to lead a technical workshop for a group of Moroccan teachers who had previously participated in the Reading Wikipedia in the Classroom program.

The workshop was designed to take participants beyond simply reading and editing Wikipedia and introduce them to some of the technical infrastructure and interconnected projects that make the Wikimedia ecosystem work.

For many new contributors, Wikipedia initially appears to be a website made mainly of articles and references. However, behind every article there is a much larger ecosystem of projects, tools, structured data, templates, categories, media files, and technical connections.

During the workshop, I wanted participants to discover this less visible side of Wikimedia and understand that contributing to free knowledge can take many different forms.

We discussed how Wikimedia projects communicate with each other and how a single contribution can sometimes be reused across several languages and projects.

One of the main parts of the session focused on Wikidata.

title: Wiki for Human Rights Nigeria: Write for Rights and July Virtual Session
content:
In June 2026, Wiki for Human Rights Nigeria embarked on the annual Wiki Loves Pride campaign, titled “Write for Rights,” to create articles around Nigerian LGBTIQ+ identities, people, and topics. We focused on the English, Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa Wikipedias. We successfully created 23 articles on English Wikipedia, 45 articles on Hausa Wikipedia, 45 on Igbo Wikipedia, and 24 on Yoruba Wikipedia. The articles can be found HERE. So far, we have been dwelling on what we achieved.

Since then, we have also collated and announced the results on the Meta page, and they can be found here. One key learning moment during the campaign is that whatever you set out to achieve, you can achieve it with the right leadership. I was initially skeptical about interest because most LGBTIQ+ people might not be interested in contributing during the contest when there are no guaranteed prizes. Existing in Nigeria is already hard for queer people, and many struggle to make ends meet.

title: The market at the top of the hill, and the Wikipedia editors who went there
content:
It’s 9 in the morning, and Eloisa Larrea and I (Carla Salazar) are meeting at a halfway point in La Paz to head to the Alto Santiago de Lacaya market. Neither of us has been there before. We’re going to talk with Mrs. Lucila Cutipa, who co-founded the market and sells fried fish there. She’s also a theater actress. We got in touch with her through Erika Andia, who directs Kory Warmis, a theater group made up of actresses who work as vendors and artisans around the city.

In August 2026, Wikimedistas de Bolivia and WikiAcción Perú launched a contest called Fiesta Plurinacional: Nuestros Mercados. The idea is to add more content about markets and popular economy in both countries. So meeting Lucila seemed like a good opportunity to learn more about how markets in La Paz work and how they organize themselves. Plus, visiting her at her stall meant we could take photos of the place and talk to other vendors while we were there.

title: Charting the Journey from Tatar Sunda to the Spice Islands Expedition through WikiRempah Bandung
content:
When people hear the word spices, most immediately think of Maluku, Ternate, Tidore, Banda, or the centuries-old trade routes that connected the Indonesian archipelago with Europe.

Yet the history of spices does not belong solely to Eastern Indonesia. In Tatar Sunda (the Sundanese homeland), spices have long been part of everyday life, from home cooking and traditional medicine to the expressions and vocabulary preserved in the Sundanese language.

Together with Hasnanf, Pijri Paijar, Adhiiik, Tanto Wijaya, and Mirani Pramitasari, Wikimedia Bandung Community continued the WikiRempah initiative launched by Ana Ainina, Supardi Sahabu, and Sofi Solihah. 

WikiRempah is an initiative funded through the Wikimedia Foundation’s Rapid Funds program and carried out in collaboration with communities supported by Wikimedia Indonesia.

During this meetup, Mirani Pramitasari also shared her knowledge about an alternative way to enable HotCat, a tool that helps registered users remove, edit, and add categories to Wikipedia pages, this time on Sundanese Wiktionary.

title: Wiki OTO 2026: A new collaboration to make African women more visible
content:
From 25 August to 25 September 2026, Wiki OTO returns to bring Wikimedia contributors together to increase the representation of African women on Wikidata.

Wiki OTO grew out of the Wiki Loves Women Focus Group, established in 2021 as a community of women Wikimedians from across Africa and beyond. As the Focus Group programme has evolved into a new format, the campaign is entering a new chapter.

For 2026, Wiki Loves Women, an initiative of Wiki in Africa, is partnering with Africa Wiki Women to organize Wiki OTO together. This collaboration brings together two communities committed to strengthening the visibility and representation of African women in free knowledge.

In Yoruba, Àrà-Ọ̀tọ̀ means “unique”, a fitting name for a campaign celebrating the women whose stories, achievements and contributions deserve to be better represented.

The 2026 edition of Wiki OTO will focus on Women in Politics, highlighting the contributions and achievements of African women in this field.
snippet: From 25 August to 25 September 2026, Wiki OTO returns to bring Wikimedia contributors together to increase the representation of African women on Wikidata.

title: Custom edit suggestions for every wiki: How communities are shaping Suggestion Mode with TextMatch
content:
Contributing to Wikipedia involves some invisible friction: finding content that needs improving, understanding what guidelines apply, and gathering the right context can all be effortful parts of the process. Suggestion Mode is a VisualEditor feature designed to reduce this friction while also helping people to publish constructive changes that they might not otherwise. It does so by proactively suggesting various types of edits one can consider making to improve content in an article.

Some of the suggestions apply broadly across all wikis, like detecting pasted text, inappropriately located external links, and images without captions. But what makes a constructive change can vary in practice beyond these shared cases. The patterns that signal a potential problem in an edit are rooted in the language, culture, and local editorial history of each project, and no single global set of suggestions can fully account for that diversity.

Rather than trying to solve this centrally, the Editing team is working to give communities the tools to define what edit suggestions would best identify these signals for their wiki.

title: Voices from the Bolivian Amazon: Madidi—My Journey to the Indigenous Communities Meeting in Wikimedia Projects
content:
EQUENE E QUEMA EJUDESHU TACANA IBUNEDHA

My connection to the Wikimedia projects began in 2024, when Eloisa Larrea Montaño, who coordinated editing workshops organized by Wikimedians from Bolivia, arrived in Tumupasa—a town located in the north of the department of La Paz, at the gateway to Madidi National Park in the Bolivian Amazon—with the goal of creating local content about the Tacana people from our own perspective and raising awareness of environmental conflicts, challenges, and projects we envision for our territory. The proposal was clear: that we ourselves, as the Tacana people, would tell our story on Wikipedia, including urgent issues such as the fires threatening our territory.

title: Six Months of Building Leaders, Bridging Knowledge Gaps, and Strengthening Community by Africa Wiki Women
content:
The first half of 2026 has been a period of remarkable growth for Africa Wiki Women (AWW). Across mentorship, leadership development, community campaigns, partnerships, and capacity building, our community has continued to create opportunities for African women to participate meaningfully in the Wikimedia movement while addressing the persistent gender gap in open knowledge.

Our work this year has gone beyond increasing contributions on Wikimedia projects. It has focused on building confident leaders, supporting new contributors, strengthening communities, and creating spaces where African women can learn, collaborate, and amplify their stories.

title: Wiki Loves Mingachevir: The Kyrgyz Wikicommunity’s Azerbaijani Adventure
content:
Held in the beautiful city of Mingachevir, Azerbaijan, from August 12-16, the Wiki Loves Mingachevir camp was an unforgettable experience in regional cooperation, knowledge sharing, and building new friendships. We represented the Kyrgyz Wikicommunity with a three-person team at this exciting event. Our participation was made possible thanks to a microgrant provided by the CEE Hub, giving us a fantastic opportunity to strengthen the bonds between our communities.

One of the highlights of the camp was the presentation on the Kyrgyz Wikicommunity, which I co-hosted with User:Ch. We shared our community’s past achievements, current general statistics, and exciting plans for the future.

The most beautiful aspect of Wikimedia events is that they offer not just a space for digital knowledge, but also for cultural exchange. To reflect this spirit, we distributed kurut (a traditional Kyrgyz dried cheese) to the participants at the end of our presentation. Tasting the kurut and the conversations it sparked added a very warm and welcoming atmosphere to the room.

title: Wikimania 2026: Impactful sessions, useful tools, and wonderful people
content:
I’m a volunteer with the Wikimedia Aotearoa New Zealand (WANZ) community, where I contribute to Wikidata, Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons. I’m also in the GLAM sector, as Curator Botany at Te Papa, the national museum of New Zealand. I attended Wikimania 2026 on an ESEAP Hub travel scholarship, and this blog is a summary of my Wikimania experience.

Wikimania 2026 was held in Paris, France from 21-25 July 2026. The theme for the conference was, “Freedom, Equity, Reliability (Liberté, Équité, Fiabilité). Together, let’s protect knowledge, equity and freedom.” About 1,200 people from over 100 countries attended in person. Sometimes there were as many as ten different and equally interesting parallel sessions, which made it difficult to choose which ones to attend. However, the sessions I chose to attend were articulate, well-prepared and worthwhile, and for I can watch those I missed on YouTube.

title: Keizo Shibusawa and Collective Intelligence: the Institute for the Study of Japanese Folk Culture Edit-a-thon
content:
On August 25, 2026, I contributed in an edit-a-thon held at the Institute for the Study of Japanese Folk Culture, Kanagawa University. The Institute collects and organizes folk artifacts and historical documents from across Japan and conducts research focusing on the society of ordinary Japanese people—including the history of the fishing industry.

The roots of the Institute lie in the Attic Museum Society, founded by Keizo Shibusawa in 1921; this organization later became the Attic Museum and was renamed the Institute for the Study of Japanese Folk Culture in 1942, during the war. Although Shibusawa took over the management of Dai-Ichi Bank at the request of his grandfather, Eiichi Shibusawa, and subsequently served as Governor of the Bank of Japan and Minister of Finance at the government’s request during and after the war. However, as he had originally aspired to a life of scholarship, he poured his passion into training many researchers, starting with folklorists.

title: Wikipedia, Digital Literacy, and Science Communication among High School Students in Brazil: Introducing NEMkipédiA
content:
On November 30, 2024, Wikimedia Brasil (WMB) participated in the VII Encontro Anual da Rede Nacional de Ciência para Educação (Rede CpE) (7th Annual Meeting of the National Science for Education Network). The event celebrated the tenth anniversary of the Rede CpE, an initiative that brings together researchers from different fields of knowledge to share scientific studies that contribute to better educational practices and policies. That year, the event also included the III Simpósio Satélite da Cátedra UNESCO de Ciência para Educação (3rd Satellite Symposium of the UNESCO Chair in Science for Education) as part of its program.

As a result of our participation, we received an honorable mention for the research we presented, titled Wikiversidade: uma plataforma para grupos de pesquisa e ciência aberta (Wikiversity: A Platform for Research Groups and Open Science). The study investigated the challenges and opportunities of Wikiversity for Brazilian scientific production and dissemination and was based on an article published on Wikiversity.

title: From Slovenia to Armenia: A WikiCamp, a Peer Exchange, and New Connections
content:
The Wikimedia movement is built on collaboration, sharing experiences, and learning from one another. So when the CEE Hub announced its Peer Learning Exchange, Wikimedia Armenia was excited to take part.

The idea of the exchange was simple: bring a developing Wikimedia community closer to a more established one, creating an opportunity to learn from each other’s experiences, share best practices, and build connections that could continue beyond the exchange itself.

Our exchange brought us together with Nal Mencin from the Wikipedians of Slovenia User Group. Once we started discussing what the exchange could look like, one activity immediately stood out: Wikimedia Armenia’s Summer Youth WikiCamp.

The WikiCamp seemed like the perfect opportunity for Nal to experience our community from the inside. Rather than simply observing how we work, we wanted him to become part of it. So, the exchange combined meetings and discussions with the Wikimedia Armenia team with something much more hands-on: becoming a WikiCamp participant.

From the very beginning, we wanted Nal to experience the WikiCamp not as an observer, but as a real participant.
